facts.raw_span: intractable mucocutaneous lesions that had been evolving for 10 years
No swollen cervical and axillary lymph nodes were palpable
Small bullae, erosions, and crusts were present on the lower lip
Erosions with epithelized mucosa were observed in the oral cavity
Flaccid discrete and coalesced bullae, crusts, and erosions over erythematous and cicatricial lesions were present on the face, trunk, and extremities
Chest, abdomen, and pelvic computed tomography showed no abnormalities
Gastrointestinal endoscopy and colonoscopy results identified no abnormalities
Skin biopsy revealed spongiosis and numerous neutrophils with nuclear dust in the epidermis and superficial perivascular dermatitis with predominant infiltration of lymphocytes in the dermis
No obvious deposits of IgG, IgA, and C3 to either the epithelial cell surface or the basement membrane zone
Positive for IgG autoantibodies to envoplakin (210 kDa) and periplakin (190 kDa)
Negative for Dsg1, Dsg3, and BP180 16th noncollagenous domain
Negative for BP230, type VII collagen, and desmocollins 1 to 3

concepts.why: The presence of autoantibodies to envoplakin and periplakin, as well as the clinical presentation of mucocutaneous lesions, is consistent with paraneoplastic pemphigus.

The clinical presentation of flaccid bullae, erosions, and crusts on the skin and mucous membranes is consistent with pemphigus vulgaris, although the negative results for Dsg1 and Dsg3 autoantibodies are unusual.
The clinical presentation of superficial bullae and erosions on the skin is consistent with pemphigus foliaceus, although the presence of mucous membrane involvement is atypical.

The presence of autoantibodies and the clinical presentation of bullae and erosions on the skin and mucous membranes is consistent with an autoimmune bullous dermatosis, although the specific subtype is unclear.

The presence of autoantibodies and the clinical presentation of bullae and erosions on the skin is consistent with epidermolysis bullosa acquisita, although the negative results for type VII collagen autoantibodies are unusual.

rationales.F01: Mucocutaneous lesions are common in various autoimmune bullous dermatoses.
rationales.F02: Absence of swollen lymph nodes reduces the likelihood of paraneoplastic pemphigus.
rationales.F03: Mucosal involvement is characteristic of pemphigus vulgaris and paraneoplastic pemphigus.
rationales.F04: Oral mucosal erosions are common in pemphigus vulgaris and paraneoplastic pemphigus.
rationales.F05: Skin lesions are present in various autoimmune bullous dermatoses.
rationales.F08: Skin biopsy findings are consistent with an autoimmune bullous dermatosis.
rationales.F10: Autoantibodies to envoplakin and periplakin are characteristic of paraneoplastic pemphigus.

frontier_selector.rationale: Positive for IgG autoantibodies to envoplakin and periplakin, which are characteristic of paraneoplastic pemphigus, despite the absence of detectable lymphadenopathy or internal malignancy.
